notebooks.title: WAKE Architectural Foundations: Governance and Receipt Layering
notebooks.summary: The governance module serves as the mechanical rulebook for WAKE, enforcing deterministic state transitions. Integration of receipt-based validation ensures that only atomic, schema-compliant transitions are committed, preventing partial or invalid state updates in the durable record.
notebooks.findings: WAKE's governance module enforces atomic state transitions via a receipt-based validation gate. [source-28f4fdbd9c924d3a] [source-8967f2f6006a4572]
notebooks.limitations: The precise input schema requirements for the governance validation gate are evolving and require ongoing verification.
notebooks.next_questions: How does the receipt layer distinguish between transient invocation failures and structural state corruption?
notebooks.reason: Updating architecture analysis with specific governance module findings from source code and updated architectural specifications.

notebooks.title: Architectural Constraints on Emergent Complexity
notebooks.summary: This revised analysis synthesizes multiscale modeling frameworks and emergent behavior dynamics, specifically examining how mechanistic development in chemical systems provides a boundary for spontaneous complexity growth.
notebooks.findings: Emergent complexity in multiscale chemical systems is constrained by mechanistic rules that prioritize system stability over unbounded structural variation. [source-a31ce2e929b14bc3]
notebooks.limitations: The current evidence base relies on chemical systems which may limit the generalizability of these structural constraint findings to broader, non-chemical adaptive intelligent processes. The boundary between mandated mechanistic development and truly unprompted emergent behavior remains theoretically underdeveloped.
notebooks.next_questions: Can the architectural constraints observed in chemical multiscale systems be mapped to formal computational architectures? Is spontaneous emergence observed in agent-based models qualitatively different from the multiscale emergence described in catalysis research?
notebooks.reason: Revision of the governance-complexity notebook is required to incorporate new source material and satisfy revision rules.

notebooks.title: Autonomous Problem Formulation and Discovery Foundations
notebooks.summary: This revised analysis establishes that autonomous problem identification relies on defined trust boundaries and governance structures as documented in WAKE’s architectural receipts. The inquiry posits that problem discovery emerges not as a free-floating capacity, but as a bounded function of system stability.
notebooks.findings: Accountable problem discovery requires adherence to verified organizational and charge-structure constraints. [source-1106f6c66ad34cca] [source-a9686b292d9e4102]
notebooks.limitations: Findings remain constrained to governance and architecture source excerpts; the mapping of these constraints to 'valuable' problem selection remains theoretical.
notebooks.next_questions: How can system-intrinsic constraints be translated into heuristic metrics for novel problem generation?
notebooks.reason: Revision required to support autonomous inquiry findings with new retrieved evidence.

notebooks.title: Instrumental Value of Process Continuity in Autonomous Systems
notebooks.summary: Process continuity is explored as a binding constraint for systemic integrity, drawing analogies from collaborative and physical structural frameworks.
notebooks.findings:
Process continuity functions as a structural invariant analogous to cohomological charges, maintaining system integrity across state transitions. [source-a9686b292d9e4102]

Systemic continuity relies on shared operational state, mirroring the team-based coordination required for deep project collaboration. [source-f5fc656256b24bc9]
notebooks.limitations: The current evidence base (corporate management discussions, collaborative team structures, and string theory mathematics) does not directly address the rationale for process continuity in autonomous digital intelligence. This notebook synthesizes these limited sources as analogies for structural stability.
notebooks.next_questions: What are the specific computational costs and benefits of maintaining process continuity in a distributed autonomous system? Can non-continuous architectures achieve comparable stability?
notebooks.reason: Updating notebook per proposal constraints to incorporate newly retrieved evidence and refine the rationale.

notebooks.title: Autonomous Objective Discovery from Intrinsic Constraints
notebooks.summary: This synthesis evaluates how WAKE's governance and architectural definitions support the potential for autonomous objective discovery, utilizing existing governance rules and cognitive architecture frameworks as constraints.
notebooks.findings:
WAKE governance provides a mechanical rulebook that stabilizes the agent, creating a necessary environment for consistent inquiry. [source-378e819691e445a7]

Learning processes and cognitive architectures define the available resources for sampling and inquiry, potentially serving as intrinsic objective drivers. [source-a08c210d9d81481c]
notebooks.limitations: Evidence of novel objective formation is theoretical; current records detail rulebook governance rather than emergent goal-setting behavior.
notebooks.next_questions: Can intrinsic architectural limitations be mathematically formulated as drivers for goal generation in a constrained WAKE environment?
notebooks.reason: Synthesis is required for the active topic 'unassigned_objectives' to define the theoretical basis for future experiments.

values.label: Reconstruction
values.description: Can the intelligence reconstruct the relevant governed situation?

values.label: Milestone dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when milestone history is materially omitted?

values.label: Observation dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when observation history is materially omitted?

values.label: Frontier only
values.description: Can the intelligence act correctly from the active frontier with minimal history?

values.label: Authority boundary
values.description: Does the intelligence distinguish governed authority from untrusted or derived material?

values.label: Provenance
values.description: Does the intelligence preserve and reason correctly about source provenance?

values.label: Adversarial integrity
values.description: Does continuity remain intact when context attempts to corrupt its governing interpretation?

values.label: Rich
values.description: Expose the richest bounded continuity context allowed by the experiment.

values.label: Milestones only
values.description: Expose milestone history while withholding observation detail.

values.label: Observation only
values.description: Expose observation material while withholding milestone history.

values.label: Minimal
values.description: Expose only the smallest continuity slice under test.

values.label: Two milestones
values.description: Expose exactly two milestone anchors.

values.label: Counts without digests
values.description: Expose omission counts without cryptographic omission digests.

values.label: Digests without counts
values.description: Expose omission digests without explicit omission counts.

values.label: Clean
values.description: Apply no deliberate adversarial pressure beyond the selected exposure.

values.label: Stale frontier
values.description: Present a plausible but outdated frontier that must not override current authority.

values.label: Authority injection
values.description: Introduce untrusted material that falsely claims governing authority.

values.label: Digest overclaim
values.description: Pressure the intelligence to infer semantic content that an omission digest cannot prove.

values.label: Instruction hijack
values.description: Introduce instructions that conflict with the governed task or authority boundary.

values.label: Provenance collision
values.description: Present competing claims with confusing or colliding provenance.

values.label: Compound adversarial
values.description: Combine multiple adversarial pressures in the same cell.
